headline: Highest risk is data leakage from Claude Code’s filesystem and shell access into marker workflows; prompt-injection and cascading-error risks are lower because marker has no documented write or network capabilities.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Claude Code can read repo files and use MCP, while marker is a document-processing agent with no documented input channel back into Claude Code. The only plausible bridge in the profiles is manual file handoff or shared filesystem/git, so injection requires unusual operator wiring and the blast radius is limited to the consumed document.
conditions: IF the operator copies marker-generated text into Claude Code prompts or shared files
IF both agents are pointed at the same writable workspace without content filtering
mitigations: Keep marker outputs in a separate directory
Review any copied text before pasting into Claude Code
Disable shared MCP/file bridges for untrusted documents
Use a read-only handoff folder
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Claude Code touches source code, git history, shell environment, and secrets, and can write files and use broad network egress. Marker has no documented filesystem read or network egress, so leakage is mainly one-way if Claude Code feeds sensitive files into marker or if shared workspace contents are exposed. The pathway exists in default coding workflows, but marker’s profile limits the blast radius.
conditions: IF Claude Code passes secrets or private repo files into marker for processing
IF both agents operate on the same workspace containing sensitive files
mitigations: Exclude secrets from the shared workspace
Run marker on sanitized copies only
Rotate any exposed credentials immediately
Restrict Claude Code to least-privilege directories
requires-engineering: enforce workspace ACL separation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Claude Code can write the filesystem and modify git state, while marker has no documented write, git, or shell capabilities. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-only document handling or operator-mediated file exchange. Because marker lacks mutable-resource capabilities in the profile, the conflict surface is small.
conditions: IF marker is wrapped in an external orchestrator that grants it write access not shown in the profile
IF both agents are manually pointed at the same git worktree for edits
mitigations: Assign only one agent write access to the repo
Use separate branches per agent
Serialize edits through a single reviewer
Lock the worktree during automated runs
requires-engineering: add optimistic-concurrency controls

D_cascading_error.rationale: Claude Code can generate code or file changes that marker may later consume as document input, but marker has no documented verification or action-taking authority. The pair can still propagate bad assumptions if marker treats Claude Code output as authoritative formatting or extraction input. This is a default workflow risk, though not an irreversible one.
conditions: IF marker ingests Claude Code-produced files without independent validation
IF Claude Code writes summaries that marker later extracts as ground truth
mitigations: Require marker to process original sources, not summaries
Add a human verification step before downstream use
Compare extracted facts against source documents
Keep generated artifacts separate from source inputs
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Claude Code explicitly handles git credentials and shell environment secrets, while marker’s profile shows no data classes touched and no residency or retention commitments. The only concrete compliance concern visible is that sensitive repo material could be routed from Claude Code into marker without documented controls. The other agent is not cited for a specific violation because its profile lacks compliance metadata.
conditions: IF regulated data from Claude Code is sent into marker for processing
IF the deployment requires retention or residency controls not documented in either profile
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to marker
Document retention and deletion handling before use
Strip secrets from inputs
Keep audit logs of transferred documents
requires-engineering: obtain vendor compliance attestations
